items.text: The study examines reverse lymphoid-to-stromal interactions in the already formed thymus, uses inducible growth without host preconditioning to separate injury from growth processes, and develops a dynamic understanding based on growth stages.

Regionally and temporally matched tissue and lymphoid expression, along with a searchable candidate database that retains itemized evidence, can generate prioritized hypotheses and reusable resources without locking into a single pathway.

A small number of existing genetic models validate biological relevance at the organ level, connecting discovery to subsequent mechanistic studies; R21 grants do not treat complete dissection of all proliferation/differentiation/survival pathways as a success criterion.

Computational subtraction of regionally mixed expression is affected by changes in cell composition, total RNA, and proportions, and cannot automatically be equated with expression changes within a specific stromal cell type; paired subtraction mitigates but does not fully resolve this.

Co-expression, co-citation, and STRING support are not equivalent to functional receptor-ligand interactions; thresholds, literature popularity, and resource availability can alter candidate ranking, and current single-cell data could supplement comparisons.

Reduced whole-organ size or transplant growth may arise from donor colonization/lymphoid development or innate developmental effects, rather than designated lymphoid-to-stromal signals; validation is also constrained by candidate dependence and the two-year workload.
